name: Dominican Republic
summary: Spain, France, Haiti, independence—and back to Spain.
notes: This is eastern Hispaniola. Toussaint Louverture acted in France’s name in 1801, before Haiti existed as an independent state. The 1965–1966 U.S./OAS intervention is an annotation, not an annexation.

events.title: Spain claims Hispaniola
events.detail: Columbus asserted Spanish sovereignty over an inhabited island.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Spanish colonization begins
events.detail: The renewed expedition established La Isabela; colonial conquest followed.

events.title: Spain cedes Santo Domingo
events.detail: The Treaty of Basel awarded the eastern colony to France; Spanish administration continued until 1801.

events.title: Louverture takes the eastern colony
events.detail: His army ended Spanish administration and abolished slavery in the name of the French Republic.

events.title: Direct French military rule
events.detail: Napoleon’s expedition replaced Louverture’s authority; the eastern colony remained French.

events.title: The Reconquista succeeds
events.detail: Spanish-aligned forces, supported by Britain, ended French rule. Rebellion began in 1808; the capital fell in 1809.

events.title: A short-lived independence
events.detail: The former Spanish colony declared independence and sought union with Gran Colombia; union did not take effect.

events.title: Boyer unifies Hispaniola
events.detail: Haitian government incorporated the east and abolished slavery there.

events.title: The Dominican Republic emerges
events.detail: A separatist movement declared independence from Haiti.

events.title: Santana arranges Spanish annexation
events.detail: President Pedro Santana invited Spain to resume sovereignty.

events.title: The Restoration War begins
events.detail: Dominican resistance fought to end renewed Spanish rule.

events.title: Independence restored
events.detail: Spain abandoned annexation after the Restoration War.
events.uncertainty: Spain revoked annexation in May; evacuation continued into July. Year precision avoids conflating the two.

events.title: U.S. military government imposed
events.detail: U.S. landings in May were followed by a formal military government in November.

events.title: Dominican government restored
events.detail: The U.S. military administration ended and troops withdrew.

events.title: U.S. intervention returns
events.detail: U.S. and later inter-American forces intervened in the civil war; withdrawal was completed in 1966.
